newsitem.title: VATICAN: Vatican cardinal reaffirms ban on women priests.
newsitem.headline: Vatican cardinal reaffirms ban on women priests.

text.p: The Vatican reaffirmed the Roman Catholic Church's ban on women priests on Friday and said theologians and members of the faithful who opposed it were committing a serious doctrinal error.

"In the strict sense this (supporting a female priesthood) would not be heresy but erroneous doctrine," Cardinal Joseph Ratzinger, head of the Vatican department that oversees doctrinal matters, said in response to a question.
Ratzinger, addressing a news conference, was discussing the case of Sri Lankan priest Tissa Balasuriya, who was excommunicated last month for heresy.
Balasuriya was the first theologian in the world to be branded a heretic in nearly half a century.
He wrote a book, "Mary and Human Liberation", which raised questions about the doctrine of original sin, the necessity of baptism and the uniqueness of Jesus Christ.

Balasuriya also supported a female priesthood. But Ratzinger said the heresy condemnation and the excommunication were inflicted after the priest refused to sign a statement renouncing all his various positions, particularly his rejection of the dogma of original sin.
At the news conference the Vatican presented a new series of books on theological topics.
The first book was dedicated to the Church's position on women in society and restating why they cannot become priests.
The Vatican says Pope John Paul's 1994 ruling against the ordination of women as priests is a definitive and infallible part of Catholic teaching.

The Church says it cannot allow women priests because Christ willingly chose only men as his apostles. Women's groups have contested this, saying Christ was merely acting according to the social norms of his times.
